audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer mentions that Graves' bullets cannot pass through units, or that he has to reload.
audit.why: New Destiny is the whole reason a ranged champion can lane into Graves: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units.' Standing so your own minion wave is between you and Graves eats most of a buckshot. And because he runs out of ammo and must reload, there is a recurring window with no auto-attack threat at all. The entry instead tells the player only to 'stay outside his shotgun cone', which is vaguer and misses both mechanics. This is the highest-value omission in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Keep your own minions between you and Graves — his four bullets do not pass through units, so the wave absorbs the burst. And every reload is a free auto for you.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (P New Destiny: 'He must reload when he runs out of ammo. Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units.')

audit.whatIsWrong: The armour is attributed to his passive in four places: whys[0] "Graves' passive gives him bonus armor per buckshot stack", whys[2] "his passive armor is also stacking", spikes[3].text "before Graves stacks his passive armor", wants.foe[1] "Stack his passive armor quickly".
audit.why: New Destiny has no armour component at all — it is the ammo and bullet-spread mechanic. The resistances come from True Grit on Quickdraw (E): he gains an Armor and Magic Resist boost on the dash, two stacks if he dashes toward a champion, and 'Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown of this skill and refreshes the resistance boost'. Putting it on the passive makes it look unavoidable; putting it where it belongs turns it into something Teemo directly counters, because a blind stops the landed autos that refresh it.
audit.corrected: His armour and MR come from True Grit on Quickdraw, refreshed by landed basic attacks. Blind those autos and you stop the refresh and delay the next dash at the same time.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (P New Destiny — no resistances; E Quickdraw: 'dashes forward gaining an Armor and Magic Resist boost... Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown of this skill and refreshes the resistance boost')

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] says "Smoke Screen can flip your Q blind back on you" and wants.foe[2] says "Use Smoke Screen to blind YOU — countering Blinding Shot by making your own auto-poke miss during his burst window".
audit.why: Smoke Screen does not blind. It creates a cloud that reduces sight range, plus impact damage and a brief slow. Attacks made from inside it do not miss — you simply cannot see out. Telling a Teemo his autos will whiff inside the smoke will make him disengage from trades he was winning.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen cuts your vision and slows on impact; it does not make your attacks miss. Treat it as a fog you should not fight blind inside, not as a counter-blind.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (W Smoke Screen: 'creating a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range. Enemies caught in the initial impact are dealt magic damage and have their Move Speed reduced briefly', flags projectile/slow/zone — no blind)

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it: "NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere". Neither layer states a number, and whys[1] actively misstates the shape — "his Quickdraw is on a long cooldown, your Q is on a long cooldown".
audit.why: Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank. That is not a long cooldown and the two are not symmetric: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12 and Smoke Screen is 26/24/22/20/18. At rank 1 you get two blinds per Quickdraw and nearly four per Smoke Screen. The concrete sequencing rule is: wait for Quickdraw to be spent before committing anything, and remember that landing autos on you is how he shortens it — so the blind is both the defensive tool and the thing that keeps his dash down.
audit.corrected: Wait for Quickdraw (16s at rank 1) to be spent before you commit. Blinding his autos denies the cooldown refund, so a blinded Graves waits the full duration.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags: "level chart contradicts data: Teemo wins 53.4% but the chart gives Graves 4/7 stages vs 0". content win[] is [Graves, Skill, Skill, Graves, Skill, Graves, Graves] while the full layer's phases[] reads [Skill, Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Skill, Teemo, Teemo].
audit.why: A chart that awards Teemo zero of seven stages cannot coexist with a 53.4% win rate over 1809 games, and the full layer already disagrees with it. Levels 2 and 3 are the two stages that are demonstrably Teemo's and are currently marked Skill: Quickdraw is 16 seconds at rank 1 against a flat 7-second blind, Graves' bullets are blocked by the minion wave, and he has to reload. The entry's own spikes[3] text already argues this stage is where Teemo banks an attrition lead. I did not touch the Graves-marked stages — his level 1 point-blank burst, his 4-5 all-in and his item spikes are genuinely his, and the entry is right that the win rate comes from attrition rather than duelling.
audit.corrected: win[1] Skill -> Teemo and win[2] Skill -> Teemo, giving Graves 4 / Teemo 2 / Skill 1 instead of Graves 4 / Teemo 0 / Skill 3.
sources: scratchpad packet teemo.json entry graves defects[0]

edits.before: Graves' passive gives him bonus armor per buckshot stack, and his level 1 auto burst is the highest in the game at close range — he controls the very first minion wave with raw damage before your poison compounds.
edits.after: Graves' passive is ammo, not armour — four bullets that cannot pass through units, so your own minion wave eats his buckshot. His close-range burst still owns the first wave, but only if you let him stand next to you.

edits.before: Both of you have one ability online — his Quickdraw is on a long cooldown, your Q is on a long cooldown. Whoever wastes their key tool first loses the trade, so the window is genuinely even.
edits.after: Both of you have one ability online, but the cooldowns are not symmetric — Quickdraw is 16 seconds at rank 1 and your blind is a flat 7. Bait the dash and you own the next nine seconds outright.

edits.before: Your poison stacks compound over three waves but his passive armor is also stacking — the attrition is roughly matched, and neither of you can force a decisive all-in without committing a key cooldown.
edits.after: Your poison compounds over three waves while his armour comes only from True Grit on Quickdraw, not from a passive — and blinding his autos stops him refreshing either the resistances or the dash.

edits.before: Graves owns Levels 4-5: Quickdraw lets him close your range advantage instantly, his buckshot point-blank burst ignores your kite pattern, and Smoke Screen can flip your Q blind back on you — stay near your tower.
edits.after: Graves owns Levels 4-5: Quickdraw closes your range advantage instantly and his point-blank burst ignores your kite pattern. Smoke Screen does not blind you — it cuts your sight range — but fighting inside it is still his call.

edits.before: Graves hits harder at level 1 than any ADC has a right to — his point-blank buckshot auto crits for enormous damage before you have any items, so never stand chest-to-chest to trade. Poke from max E range: let the poison tick while you stay outside his shotgun cone. At level 2 and 3 he still has Quickdraw on a long cooldown — chip him with E autos, fire Q the instant he dashes in, and immediately W back out. You are not going to bully him out of lane; you are setting a small HP lead that your mushrooms will protect later.
edits.after: Graves hits harder at level 1 than any ADC has a right to, so never stand chest-to-chest. His bullets cannot pass through units, so keep your own minions between you and him and most of that buckshot never arrives. Poke from max E range and let the poison tick. He also has to reload when his ammo runs out — that gap is a free auto for you every single time. At levels 2-3 Quickdraw is 16 seconds against your flat 7-second blind: chip with E autos, blind the instant he dashes in, and W back out.

edits.before: At levels 4 and 5 Graves becomes genuinely dangerous: he can dash in, dump a full combo, and dash back out before your Q blind even matters much — his burst window is shorter than your cast time if he catches you flat-footed. Respect his all-in range and keep the wave near your tower so he burns Quickdraw to engage and has no dash to escape your Q. At level 6 the map tips back your way: drop mushrooms in every brush and at both jungle entrances so his Quickdraw destinations are pre-poisoned, slowed, and revealed. He cannot side-step a mushroom he never saw.
edits.after: At levels 4 and 5 Graves becomes genuinely dangerous: he can dash in, dump a full combo, and dash back out before your blind matters much. But Quickdraw only comes back faster when his basic attacks land, so every blind you hit delays both his dash and his True Grit resistances. Keep the wave near your tower so he burns Quickdraw to engage and has nothing left to escape with. At level 6 the map tips back your way: drop mushrooms in every brush and at both jungle entrances so his Quickdraw destinations are pre-poisoned, slowed and revealed. He cannot side-step a mushroom he never saw.

edits.after: Your E poison and AA poke can set a small attrition lead while Quickdraw is still 16 seconds — force trades before he can refresh True Grit off landed autos.

notes:
APPLIER LIMITATION worth knowing: the level chart for this matchup cannot be fully reconciled under the +/-10% length rule. "Graves" is 6 characters and both alternatives ("Teemo", "Skill") are 5, so 5/6 = 83% and any Graves-marked stage will be rejected. That means win[0], win[3], win[5] and win[6] are frozen as Graves no matter what the audit finds — I could only move the two Skill stages. The same trap will hit every enemy whose display name is not 5 characters (Gangplank, Gragas, Dr. Mundo, Gnar, and so on), so charts for those champions can never be corrected toward Teemo by the current applier. Either the length rule needs an exemption for win[]/phases[].side, or those fields need a separate code path. This is also why teemo__mel.json from another slice failed validation on a 3-to-5-character side swap.

Separately, I did not write anything about Q End of the Line detonating early on terrain contact. It is in the kit text ('detonates after 1 second, or after colliding with terrain') and is real Graves tech, but nothing in the current copy touches it and adding it would have meant displacing something accurate, so I left it as a note instead.
